lines.text: i.e. the Spirit, the Spirit of truth, whom His own are to
receive, and who will guide them into all truth.
Of course at this moment of the story, when events are
breaking over them, the disciples are not in a position to
understand the inner meaning of those events. "I have yet
many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now."
They have understood only one thing, namely that their
Master is about to depart from them and leave them bereft;
and their heart is filled with sadness. Their gaze is focused
on what is visibly happening around them with a tangible
impact on themselves; and therefore they are bewildered
and in despair. The new insight which the Spirit of truth
will bestow on them consists in this, that their eyes will be
opened to the invisible aspect of events and to what con-
stitutes the real and true happening of the present hour.
This is the truth into which the Spirit is to lead them; the
reality behind the visible, which alone gives to all that is
visible its essential significance. The Spirit opens our eyes to
the invisible working of God, which is veiled by the visible
events taking place in the world. For the ultimately real
and true is not what intrudes itself on our notice, what
sets in motion our feeling, thinking and willing, what
stuns us with its terror or perhaps may thrill us with its
magnificence. No; only behind all that lies the funda-
mentally true and real, namely that which God is effecting,
and which therefore alone has true meaning for our lives.
Once the spirit has opened our eyes to this inner truth
and reality, then we shall no longer consider the visible and
apparent as the fundamental but shall measure its signifi-
cance and value in the light of what it means to God, and
we shall be able to penetrate to its innocence or false-
hood. For its significance might be much greater but also
much more trivial than we first supposed; it may be more
pleasing but also more terrifying than we surmised in the
first instance.
